slot.brief: Given E° values of M(n+1)+/Mn+ couples, arrange metals in order of reducing strength.

stem:
At $298\ \text{K}$, the standard reduction potentials are given below. Arrange the ions in decreasing order of reducing strength.

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{Cr}^{3+}(aq)+e^-&\rightleftharpoons\text{Cr}^{2+}(aq) && E^\circ=-0.41\ \text{V}\\
\text{Ti}^{3+}(aq)+e^-&\rightleftharpoons\text{Ti}^{2+}(aq) && E^\circ=-0.37\ \text{V}\\
\text{Fe}^{3+}(aq)+e^-&\rightleftharpoons\text{Fe}^{2+}(aq) && E^\circ=+0.77\ \text{V}\\
\text{Co}^{3+}(aq)+e^-&\rightleftharpoons\text{Co}^{2+}(aq) && E^\circ=+1.82\ \text{V}
\end{aligned}$$

verdicts.working: More negative E°(M³⁺/M²⁺) means M²⁺ is more readily oxidized and is the stronger reducing agent. Thus Cr²⁺ > Ti²⁺ > Fe²⁺ > Co²⁺.

working:
For $\text{M}^{3+}+e^-\to\text{M}^{2+}$, lower $E^\circ$ means $\text{M}^{2+}$ is the stronger reducing agent.
$$-0.41<-0.37<+0.77<+1.82$$
$$\text{Cr}^{2+}>\text{Ti}^{2+}>\text{Fe}^{2+}>\text{Co}^{2+}$$

Independent check: More negative E°(M³⁺/M²⁺) means M²⁺ is more readily oxidized and is the stronger reducing agent. Thus Cr²⁺ > Ti²⁺ > Fe²⁺ > Co²⁺.
